Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates patchy peripheral opacities that are more prominent in the lower lung zones, a distribution pattern classically associated with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) in patients with asthma and nasal polyposis. Although the automated tools provided conflicting or non-specific findings (guided by t000002), visual inspection confirms the lower-zone predominance described in option A, distinguishing it from the apical or central patterns of other differentials.
